propositions: Gate operations emit no incremental output at the default logging level (WARNING) between command start and final verdict, causing supervising agents' stall watchdogs to timeout while the operation is still running.

Long silent phases (27s prologue, 40s overlap retrieval, 85s to verdict) are local compute or network I/O without model calls, and are not instrumented by existing phase logs which fire only after completion at INFO level.

A synchronous keepalive helper with ~25s coalescing interval emitted at LLM-call, tool-call, and workflow-step boundaries will break the failure by bounding the worst-case silent gap to a single model round-trip.

Keepalive emission must be purely additive via logging at WARNING level to stderr, with no background daemon thread, progress-gating, stall escalation, total-runtime cap, or timeout behavior changes, preserving ADR 0089 and existing silence-tolerance tests.

Supervisor stall budgets commonly set at 600s are exceeded by multi-call gate operations that remain silent between calls; documentation must warn of this and advise raising no-output budgets accordingly.
